title: A non-radical take on how gen AI should currently be used in desktop commercial games (do whatever you want if you are a hobbyist since you are only developing for yourself)
author: KittyMeowMoo1
selftext:
I think there is too much separation of the truth between hardcore pro ai people and anti ai people, so here is my relatively neutral take on the matter.  
**AI use for programming - mostly acceptable\***  
\-AI is very useful for programming as long as you remain in complete control, understand every part of your code, and know how to maintain it from scratch without AI help. This is important for properly controlling the AI and making sure it behaves. This is also prioritized to help you not lose critical thinking skills over time.  
**AI use for design and prototyping - mostly acceptable\***  
\-Thinking on your own is incredibly important for producing a unique idea, however AI is great at helping you stick to general guidelines during design. Using AI too much during design can lead to a concept that feels flat and decreases engagement from your production. For prototyping, do whatever you want honestly. As long as you replace everything you prototype with a more polished version that you completely understand, you will be fine.  
**AI use for art - mostly not acceptable**  
\-The audience we are talking about here is the median Steam gamer. Some corners are not worth cutting and this is definitely one of them. I compare it to cheaping out on your power supply, sure you might not be able to afford the more expensive parts, but you just bricked every component in your PC as a result. To connect this metaphor, Steam gamers will see the AI art and associate that cut corner with the rest of the game.  
**AI use for music - mostly not acceptable**  
\-Same points as above. Music is with art on being a major first impression for your consumers. If you can't make music, you have to pay the price of contracting or your reputation could be seriously hurt on Steam for a larger game. AI art and music fundamentally miss the point of how I think statistical tools like gen AI should be utilized. It's like a fish trying to climb a tree ya know? I think the technology is just being shoved into things where it does not belong in devving.  


**summary -** with every new technology, people try to shove it into things where it doesn't belong, and it causes ethical problems and community divide. Don't be afraid to develop with new technologies but always be critical on the matter, not radical!  


**my biased take -** ok that was what I think the general people should follow for a successful game, for me, I completely avoid the use of AI except for sometimes using the vscode autofill or quick fix tool (and I am only using it in extreme moderation and not even in my current commercial game). **This does not mean I hate on people who use AI**, I am just doing what I think benefits me as an individual the most

comments.body: I find this post mostly not acceptable.

comments.author: GaiusVictor
comments.body:
I'm really sorry but I feel a conversation that starts with the goal of decreasing polarization, but still tries to determine what kind of tool is acceptable or not, is bound to fail on its goal.

I feel we'd need to analyze your objections here.

On your "**AI use for art**" and "**AI use for music**" sections you talk about how customers will see AI art or hear AI music and immediately assume we cut corners and that the dev has cheapened out. You frame it as a purely pragmatical/commercial stance: "This is how your customers will see it"

But do you think we don't know it beforehand? It's absolutely impossible to have not seen AI hate in the Western part of the internet, so pretty much all the devs who are here are very aware that we're already losing a good chunk of potential clients when we choose to use AI. This really feels like saying "the water is wet". We know, and we still chose to dive into the water.

Then on your **summary** you say:

>people try to shove it into things where it doesn't belong, and it causes ethical problems and community divide

This makes things even more confusing. Why do you think AI use on visual/audio assets is unacceptable? Is it because of market reasons (customers disliking it)? Or is it because of ethical reasons/because you feel AI doesn't belong? It's really hard to look at this argument and not believe it's an attempt to just convince people that "AI art bad" instead of trying to dimish polarization.

And who is trying to "shove it" into things where it doesn't belong? We? Who are just making our games and not forcing anyone to buy or play them?

That really makes this post even less effective at decreasing polarization, I feel.

My personal opinion is usually on the other direction and aligns with advice I give to people: Make your AI art good. Know the tools you have available to you, and don't use the cheap/simple ones. Establish a workflow. Study art theory (perspective, shape theory, color theory, etc), as that can really elevate your AI art. Hell, I even tell people to learn the basics of a non-AI artform so they can use it to guide their AI generations and manually correct any mistakes they make.

I personally am still figuring out the exact workflow and art style I'll use on my game. Since I also know 3D (was making 3D art even before I generated my first image), my initial plan was to use 3D models and animations to guide the AI generations and thus solve/eliminate many of the usual AI issues, but I've given up on that route due to aesthetic reasons. I think I'll use the 3D models as loose references for AI-generated character sprites and then I'll rig them and animate them by hand. I got no experience with 2D rig animation yet, but I learned 3D art and AI art, so I can learn another one.
